item.title: Trump's U.N. ambassador says Iran war could drag on for another year
item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.title: Iran has "increased efforts to target U.S. personnel," intel chief warns
item.description: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned in a memo to Secretary of State Rubio that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel," and the plots have "reached advanced stages."

item.title: DOJ demands that some California counties set aside alleged noncitizen ballots
item.description: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Justice Department said may belong to noncitizens.

item.title: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
item.description: The Trump administration is suing to prevent the Alaska Senate election from being certified if GOP Sen. Daniel Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola because of the other Dan Sullivan who is on the ballot.

item.title: Melania Trump secures "temporary ceasefire" in Ukrainian city
item.description: First lady Melania Trump's office says she secured a localized ceasefire for the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky.

item.title: Thune campaigns with Ashley Hinson as Senate GOP zeroes in on Iowa
item.description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune campaigned with GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa on Friday in his latest effort to prop up Republican candidates on the campaign trail.

item.title: Roller coaster safety experts weigh in on Six Flags investigation
item.description: The Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia has been closed since a man died after witnesses say he was ejected from the ride.

item.title: Justice Department attempts to block certification of Alaska Senate race if Republican loses
item.description: President Trump is calling into question the integrity of the upcoming Alaska Senate vote, asking the Justice Department to block future certification over possible confusion around the identities of two candidates who share the same name. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Indiana school bus driver gets children out of bus just before it goes up in flames
item.description: An Indiana resident captured footage of the moment when a school bus was consumed by flames, leaving only the frame, just after the student passengers were let out. Tom Hanson has the details.

item.title: New book, "Formula 101," gives fans a crash course on F1 racing
item.description: Matt Elisofon and Brian Muller are the hosts of "The Red Flags" podcast and have a new book coming out called "Formula 101." They say it's got something for everyone who has any level of interest in F1 racing. Elisofon and Muller join CBS News to discuss the book.

item.title: "The Kindness Mob" has come to the rescue of hundreds of online bullying victims
item.description: Started in 2023, "The Kindness Mob" is a group about half a million strong that secretly battles internet spite.

item.title: Meghan Markle responds as estranged father investigated for alleged child porn posession
item.description: Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, said in a statement Friday that she's "deeply distressed" by reports that her father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation in the Philippines for alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials. CBS News reporter Emmet Lyons has more.

item.title: New 60 Minutes report on "third-country deporations"
item.description: Within five days of being deported from the U.S., Moussa Diawara says Ghanaian officials forced him onto a flight to Mali, the very country a U.S. immigration judge ruled he could not be deported to. Diawara says he was homeless and went into hiding. Watch the 60 Minutes report Sunday at 7 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and streaming on Paramount+.

item.title: NASA outlines revised 2028 Artemis moon landing campaign
item.description: NASA will not make a decision on whether to use a SpaceX or Blue Origin moon lander until testing shows which one is the obvious choice.

item.title: Woman bullied for posting weight loss video receives flood of support from kind strangers
item.description: "The Kindness Mob," a group of half-a-million people, is helping online strangers recover from hate comments. Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" to meet one woman who benefited from the mob's help.

item.title: Hero dad who stopped Oregon school shooter shares his story
item.description: 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco shared his story with Oregon Public Broadcasting a week after the school shooting that killed three children and a teacher.

item.title: Man accused of decapitating Iwo Jima WWII statue in Virginia
item.description: A man was arrested on allegations he decapitated a World War II statue at an Iwo Jima Memorial in Quantico, Virginia, this week using a sledgehammer. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Legal expert on DOJ lawsuit to block certification of Alaska Senate election if Republican loses
item.description: President Trump's Justice Department has filed a lawsuit to block the certification of Alaska's Senate race if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It argues the presence of another GOP candidate, named Daniel J. Sullivan, could create confusion for voters and benefit Democrats. CBS news legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks it all down.

item.title: Police officer who shot and killed 1-year-old resigns
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general's office had determined that the use of force was justified in the deadly shooting that stemmed from an alleged shoplifting incident.

item.title: What to expect from Brewers-Rays World Series
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are set to host the Tampa Bay Rays Friday night in Game 1 of the World Series. Levi Weaver, staff writer for the Athletic, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: France to deploy 70,000 police officers Saturday as it prepares for more mass protests
item.description: The police presence is being boosted across France as it braces for another weekend of anti-government protests. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry has more.

item.title: 60 Minutes investigates "third-country deportations"
item.description: As the Trump administration seeks to carry out the largest deportation in American history, it is removing more and more people to countries they are not from and often have no ties to. It's called "third-country deportation." A 60 Minutes investigation reveals how some of these third countries are forcing deportees back to the nations they fled, places where U.S. immigration judges have ruled they could not be sent because they'd likely face persecution or torture.

item.title: Colorado, Utah contend with heavy flooding
item.description: Multiple states are dealing with severe weather, including flooding and gusty winds. Rob Marciano has the details.

item.title: How Thomas Jefferson politicked his way into the Louisiana Purchase
item.description: The Louisiana Purchase was the biggest territorial expansion in American history. A new book, "Jefferson's Landmark Deal," examines the unique role President Thomas Jefferson played in that monumental acquisition. Author and public scholar Lara Brown, who is also Major Garrett's wife, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: 10/23: CBS Evening News
item.description: This dad stopped the Oregon school shooting; Officer who fatally shot 1-year-old resigns.

item.title: Democrat hoping to flip Nebraska House seat pushing for action on affordability
item.description: One of the congressional seats Democrats are eyeing as a potential flip is Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District. Candidate Denise Powell joins "The Takeout" to discuss her priorities if elected to the House.

item.title: Top Ukrainian diplomat says SpaceX satellite access is still restricted
item.description: Ukrainian officials say their access to the SpaceX satellite service remains restricted, despite President Trump's claim that Elon Musk has fully restored access. Denys Sienik, Chargé d'Affaires at the Embassy of Ukraine in the U.S., joins to discuss that and the temporary ceasefire first lady Melania Trump helped secure in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city.

item.title: UFO files detail strange, silent triangular craft: "Absolute acoustic silence"
item.description: Federal agents encountered a large aircraft that zoomed across the sky from a standstill while making no noise or giving off any exhaust, according to new files.

item.title: ICE crackdown prompts some Texas Latinos to turn away from Trump
item.description: "I regret my vote for Biden. Now I regret my vote for Trump," one man said. "What other options do we got?"

item.title: Meghan "deeply distressed" as dad faces child abuse material probe
item.description: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is facing a probe in the Philippines over alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.
